text:
alexa: Heads-up — ran into a weird issue on Windows with the new MSI: redwoodctl exits with "failed to lock profiles store" right after install. happens only when Defender quarantines the exe.

noah: oh no. Defender flagged it? what's the detection name?

alexa: Windows Defender shows threat: PUA:InstallerStub. It quarantines C:\\Program Files\\Redwood\\redwoodctl.exe, but the installer still writes config files to C:\\ProgramData\\Redwood\\profiles.json. redwoodctl then can't open the exe path and fails trying to create a lock file.

toni: interesting. we only test installer on clean VMs. didn't simulate AV quarantines. rough when people install on corp laptops. any logs?

alexa: here's the tail of the log (from %LOCALAPPDATA%\\Temp\\redwood-install.log):

```
2026-03-10T14:02:11Z INFO writing profiles to C:\\ProgramData\\Redwood\\profiles.json
2026-03-10T14:02:11Z ERROR failed to acquire lock on C:\\Program Files\\Redwood\\profiles.lock: access denied
2026-03-10T14:02:11Z FATAL cannot initialize profiles store: open C:\\Program Files\\Redwood\\redwoodctl.exe: no such file or directory
```

noah: aha. the installer assumes Program Files is writable for lock files which is wrong for per-machine installs (and also if AV quarantines). we should use a machine-writable path for locks (ProgramData) or fall back to per-user.

install-bot: Known issue logged: INST-789 windows msi: profile lock path uses Program Files, conflicts with AV/per-machine perms. Suggested mitigation: use ProgramData for lock files.

toni: mitigation options for customers in the meantime?

alexa: workarounds that helped me:
- run install with `msiexec /i redwoodctl.msi ALLUSERS=2` to force per-user install (installs to %LOCALAPPDATA% and avoids Program Files lock)
- add an exclusion in Defender for C:\\Program Files\\Redwood\\redwoodctl.exe (painful for orgs)
- run `redwoodctl --config-dir %APPDATA%\\Redwood config migrate` to move profiles to a per-user dir and set REDWOODCTL_CONFIG_DIR env var for the sample app

noah: also worth noting: the sample app `nlu-demo` shipped in the quickstart looks for profiles at %USERPROFILE%\\.redwood by default. if people install for all users it won't find profiles unless you migrate or set REDWOODCTL_CONFIG_DIR. That tripped me when pairing with an intern.

toni: can we detect when profiles are only in ProgramData and print a clear advisory to the user with steps? e.g., "Detected machine-install without accessible profile store — run this command to migrate..."

install-bot: Feature suggestion appended to INST-789: add on-install advisory + automatic per-user migration option.

alexa: small snippet I ended up adding to onboarding README for Windows devs:

```
# Windows troubleshooting
# If redwoodctl errors with "failed to lock profiles store":
msiexec /i redwoodctl.msi ALLUSERS=2
# or migrate existing machine profiles to your user dir:
set REDWOODCTL_CONFIG_DIR=%APPDATA%\\Redwood
redwoodctl config migrate --from C:\\ProgramData\\Redwood
```

noah: one more gotcha: localserve spawns a child process that tries to spawn redwoodctl for auth if no token found. when redwoodctl is quarantined or missing, localserve's error was just "auth failed" with no hint. we should bubble the underlying cause.

toni: agree — add more verbose errors for spawn failures and suggest `redwoodctl --version` as a quick check.

devex-bot: PR created: docs/windows-msi-lock-fallback (refs INST-789). Assigned to @install-team.

alexa: thanks. ticket also requested a small MSI test job on CI that runs Windows Defender scan in a sandboxed VM to catch regressions.

noah: awesome — that will save hours for new hires. :raised_hands:

toni: once install-team has a fix, let's add a note to the quickstart: Windows: prefer per-user install for devs, or set REDWOODCTL_CONFIG_DIR. Also include the nlu-demo hint about REDWOOD_PROFILE env var.

alexa: done — will follow up with a short PR to the quickstart. closing thread when PR merges.
